thread.title: Weekly Market Preview: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (BAC, NFLX, IBM, AA)

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Weekly Market Preview: Four Stocks To Watch For the Coming Week (BAC, NFLX, IBM, AA)
text:
Shutterstock photo I asked last week whether the fears of interest rate increases would rattle the stock the market. It didn’t take long for that answer to be revealed. Admittedly, while I did expect some volatility to take place, the degree of panic exceeded even my worst-case scenarios. At its worst, rate fears slashed some 1,400 points from the Dow Jones Industrial Average. Which didn’t make much sense to me.
Still, cooler heads seemingly prevailed on Friday as stocks ended the session higher after suffering for much of the week. The blue chip index ended the Friday’s session up 287.16 points to closed 25,339.99, but still losing 4.2% for the week. Snapping a six-day losing streak, the S&P 500 index gained 38.76 points 2,767.13, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq, which was briefly teetered on a verge a correction, staged a stunning reversal Friday, notching 167.83 points, or 2.3%, to 7,496.89.
Heading into this week, investors want to know, have we seen the worst of these declines? I know my 401(K) certainly hopes so. The good news is, there’s a flurry of earnings coming up that could (or should) easily take the focus off interest rates and shift sentiment back to revenue and profit growth.
Analysts remain broadly positive about the the direction of the economy and there’s still strong expectations that this will be yet another quarter of positive earnings results. Earnings growth of about 19% and revenue growth of 7% are the targets, according to FactSet data. Here are the stock’s to keep an eye on this for this week.
Bank of America ( BAC ) - Reports before the open, Monday, Oct. 15
Wall Street expects Bank of America to earn 62 cents per share on revenue of $22.67 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earning were 48 cents per share on $22.08 billion in revenue.
What to Watch: With better-than-expected earnings results released Friday from JPMorgan ( JPM ) and Citigroup ( C ), Bank of America investors are hoping for similar outcome as the bank has beaten earnings estimates in eight straight quarters. Specifically, with loan and deposit growth being among the major objectives, analysts will want to see to what extent can other parts of the business, such as investment banking, support top-line growth and sustainable profits.
Netflix ( NFLX ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, Oct. 16
Wall Street expects Netflix to earn 68 cents per share on revenue of $4.01 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earning were 29 cents per share on $2.98 billion in revenue.
What to Watch: Neflix’s Q3 results will be the first among its FAANG peers — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Apple ( AAPL ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), which have all suffered during the recent tech selloff. For Netflix, however, the movie streaming giant will look to bounce back after Q2 subscriber additions for both domestic and international, fell short of Wall Street expectations. Netflix shares fell sharply as a result. But analysts remain positive that the Q2 miss, attributed to World Cup euphoria, was not the beginning of a trend.
IBM ( IBM ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, Oct. 16
Wall Street expects IBM to earn $3.39 per share on revenue of $19.11 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earning were $3.26 per share on $19.15 billion in revenue.
What to Watch: The main question heading into the quarter is, to what extent has the company’s efforts at new-age tech, particularly in areas of technology services, cloud-platform and cognitive-solutions, ready to bear fruit. These newer businesses, which contributed to last quarter’s revenue growth, have begun to offset declines in its legacy operations. The blue chip company is attempting to transform itself for the new age, but doubters still remain.
Alcoa ( AA ) - Reports after the close, Wednesday, Oct. 17
Wall Street expects Alcoa to earn 56 cents per share on revenue of $3.34 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earning were 72 cents per share on $2.96 billion in revenue.
What to Watch: Shares of the aluminum giant have been crushed, plunging almost 20% over the past five days and are down 34% year to date. This compares to a 9% year-to-date decline in the SPDR S&P Metals & Mining ETF ( XME ). The selloff in metal stocks have been driven by the intense US-China trade war drama. And given that China is world’s largest consumer of metals, the tariffs and slowdown in Chinese demand has kept investors at arms-length of metal stocks. On Wednesday investors will look to see if Alcoa management can inject some optimism to offer a sense that the metal scare could be overblown.
